51. Uses Of H2S as analytical reagent.

Hydrogen sulphide is used in a laboratory for the separation of metal ions in groups during salt analysis. bletals ions such as Cu+2, Pb+2, Cd-2, Bi+2, Sn+4, As*3, 5, Sb•3, Sb+5 are placed in group II because their sulphides are insoluble in dil. HCl medium.

Ntetals ions such as Co•2, Ni+2, Mn*2 and Zn+2 are placed in group 111B of the salt analysis table Irn because their sulphides do not precipitate out in HCl medium but they precipitate out in ammoniacal medium in presence of NH40H and NH4CI.
Hydrogen sulphide (H2S) gas is used as analytical agent to detect group (II) ions in acidic medium i.e. dil. HCl and group (111B) ions in alkaline medium i.e.NH4Cl and NH40H.

In acidic medium: HS gas is passed through the solution of group (II) metal salts in acidic medium then characteristic coloured ppt. is obtarned. These coloured ppt. shows the presence of metal ions in given salts.

In alkaline medium: When H2S gas is passed through group (111B) metal salts in alkaline medium i.e. NH4Cl and NH40H then characteristic coloured ppt. is obtained which show the presence of metal ions.
